paper_title: Efficient Ensemble for Fine-tuning Language Models on Multiple Datasets
caption: We show the empirical generalization errors (termed Error in the figures) and estimated Hessian traces of the loss for fine-tuned adapters (using QAdapter on Llama-3-8B) across various hidden dimensions. Smaller adapters achieve the lowest generalization errors. Additionally, the Hessian trace values correlate with generalization errors, suggesting that smaller adapters tend to converge to flatter minima.
model_annotation: The line chart, titled “Errors (BoolQ),” displays the empirical generalization error on the BoolQ dataset for fine-tuned adapters using QAdapter on Llama-3-8B, plotted against the adapter’s rank, which corresponds to its hidden dimension size. The x-axis, labeled “Rank,” is linearly scaled and spans values 4, 16, 64, and 256, with tick marks at each of these discrete points. The y-axis, labeled “Errors (BoolQ),” is linearly scaled from 0.0 to 0.6 in increments of 0.2. A single black solid line connects four green circular markers, each accompanied by vertical error bars indicating variability. At rank 4, the error is approximately 0.28; it decreases slightly to 0.25 at rank 16, then increases to 0.30 at rank 64, and further rises to 0.36 at rank 256. The error bars extend approximately ±0.07 at rank 4, ±0.09 at rank 16, ±0.08 at rank 64, and ±0.06 at rank 256.

model_annotations.English: The plot illustrates the empirical generalization errors (labeled “Errors (BoolQ)”) for fine-tuned adapters on the BoolQ dataset, as a function of adapter rank — a proxy for model size — using QAdapter on Llama-3-8B. The x-axis, labeled “Rank,” is on a linear scale ranging from 4 to 256, with tick marks at 4, 16, 64, and 256. The y-axis, labeled “Errors (BoolQ),” is also linear, ranging from 0.0 to 0.6, with major ticks at 0.0, 0.2, 0.4, and 0.6. A single black solid line connects four green circular data points, each accompanied by vertical error bars indicating uncertainty. At rank 4, the error is approximately 0.28; it dips slightly to around 0.25 at rank 16, rises to about 0.30 at rank 64, and further increases to roughly 0.36 at rank 256. This trend suggests that smaller adapters (lower rank) generally achieve lower generalization errors, consistent with the paper’s claim that smaller adapters converge to flatter minima, as corroborated by the correlation with Hessian trace values mentioned in the caption.
